name: Example: Maximizing the Area of a Triangle Inscribed in a Circle
problem: Consider a right triangle inscribed in a semicircle of radius $3\sqrt{2}.$ Find the maximum possible area of the triangle.
worked_solution:
We first draw a picture of the situation:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14196324/assets/1ce7e5168c729917318b00b8ffaafaef699b9a0e447ee3493a3d76f51d9d5d92.png)

Let's call $l$ the length of one leg. By the Pythagorean theorem, the length of the other leg is $\sqrt{72-l^2}.$

Therefore, the area of the triangle is given by

$$
A(l) = \frac{1}{2}l\sqrt{72-l^2} \,.
$$

Since $l$ is the length of a leg of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is $6\sqrt{2}$, the permitted range of $l$ is $0<           l<           6\sqrt{2}.$

We want to maximize $A(l),$ so we need to compute the critical points. Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(l) & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}-\frac{{l}^{2}}{2\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

and solving $A'(l)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(l) & =0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}-\frac{{l}^{2}}{2\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}} & =0 \\ 2\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}-\frac{{l}^{2}}{2\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}}) & =2\sqrt{72-{l}^{2}}\cdot 0 \\ 72-{l}^{2}-{l}^{2} & =0 \\ {l}^{2} & =\frac{72}{2} \\ {l}^{2} & =36 \\ l & =6\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to confirm that $l=6$ does indeed give a maximum value of $A(l).$ To do this, we use the first derivative test. We write up a table of values:

| Interval | $(0,6)$ | $6$ | $(6, 6\sqrt{2})$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $1$ |  | $7$ |
| $P'$ | $\color{red}+$ | $0$ | $\color{blue}-$ |
| $P$ | $\color{red}\nearrow$ | $\textrm{max}$ | $\color{blue}\searrow$ |

So, $l=6$ does indeed give a maximum, and the area of the resulting triangle will be the largest possible.

Finally, the maximum possible area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A(6) & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot \sqrt{72-{(6)}^{2}} \\  & =3\cdot \sqrt{72-36} \\  & =3\cdot \sqrt{36} \\  & =3\cdot 6 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
